findings.title: This page tells search engines not to list it
findings.evidence:
<meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">
    on https://badseo.dev/index/noindex-meta
findings.impact: This single tag removes the page from Google entirely. It will not appear for any search, including the business’s own name. It is most often left behind from a staging site or a site that was deliberately hidden before launch and never switched back.
findings.fix: Remove `noindex` from the robots meta tag on pages that should be found. Check the whole site, not just this page, because the tag is usually applied in a shared layout or template.

findings.title: The server sends a header telling search engines not to list this page
findings.evidence:
X-Robots-Tag: noindex
    in the response to GET https://badseo.dev/index/noindex-header
findings.impact: Same effect as a noindex tag, and harder to spot because it is invisible in the page source. The page will not appear in search results.
findings.fix: Remove the `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` header from responses for public pages. It is set at the server, CDN or hosting-platform level rather than in the page itself.

findings.title: The page has no title
findings.evidence: No <title> element in the head of https://badseo.dev/head/missing-title
findings.impact: The title is the blue clickable line in search results and the label on a browser tab. Without one, Google invents something from the page content, usually badly, and the page loses its single strongest ranking signal.
findings.fix: Add a `<title>` of roughly 50–60 characters that names the page and the business, most specific part first.

findings.title: The page names more than one "official" address for itself
findings.evidence:
<link rel="canonical" href="https://badseo.dev/index/canonical-conflict?via=html">
    Link: <https://badseo.dev/index/canonical-conflict?via=header>; rel="canonical"   (HTTP header, not visible in the page source)
    on https://badseo.dev/index/canonical-conflict
findings.impact: A canonical tag tells search engines which address is the real one when several show the same content. Two conflicting tags is a contradiction, so search engines ignore both and guess, which can split the page’s ranking across duplicate addresses.
findings.fix: Emit exactly one canonical link per page, in one place. Two usually means a layout and a page template are each adding one, or that one is in the HTML while another is set as an HTTP header at the server or CDN.

findings.title: Some addresses redirect in a circle
findings.evidence:
https://badseo.dev/redirect/loop
      302 → https://badseo.dev/redirect/loop
findings.impact: The browser gives up and shows an error, so the page is unreachable for visitors and cannot be indexed at all. Usually caused by two rules disagreeing about a trailing slash or about www.
findings.fix: Pick one canonical form, with or without the trailing slash and with or without www, then make every rule redirect towards it rather than between the two.

findings.title: A page answers with a server error
findings.evidence:
GET https://badseo.dev/status/server-error
    HTTP 500
findings.impact: Visitors reaching this address see an error rather than the page. Search engines drop a page that answers this way, and if it happens across many addresses they slow down crawling the whole site. The page may still render something, which is why this is easy to miss by eye.
findings.fix: Find why the server is failing for this address and fix it. If the page has genuinely been removed, answer 404 or 410 deliberately rather than 5xx.

findings.title: The page has no main heading
findings.evidence: No <h1> found on https://badseo.dev/head/missing-h1. First heading is an <h2>: "Where the headline should be".
findings.impact: The main heading tells both a search engine and a screen-reader user what the page is about. Styling text to look like a heading is not the same thing, because only the markup is read.
findings.fix: Mark the page’s main heading as `<h1>`. One per page.

findings.title: This page points search engines at a different address
findings.evidence:
Requested: https://badseo.dev/index/canonicalized
    <link rel="canonical" href="https://badseo.dev/">
findings.impact: Search engines will show the other address instead of this one, and any links earned by this page are credited there. Correct when the pages really are duplicates; a mistake when they are not.
findings.fix: Confirm the target is genuinely the same content. If it is not, point the canonical at this page’s own address.

findings.title: A page we were asked to check does not exist
findings.evidence:
GET https://badseo.dev/status/not-found
    HTTP 404
findings.impact: This address returns "not found". If it is linked from anywhere, or was previously indexed, visitors following those links reach nothing and any ranking it held is lost.
findings.fix: Restore the page, or redirect the address to whatever replaced it with a 301 so existing links and bookmarks keep working.

findings.title: A page refuses access
findings.evidence:
GET https://badseo.dev/status/blocked
    HTTP 403
findings.impact: The server refused to serve this address to an ordinary visitor, so a search engine cannot read it either and it will not be listed. Correct for an admin or account page; a mistake for anything meant to be public.
findings.fix: If the page is meant to be public, remove whatever is refusing it: an access rule, a password, or a firewall. If it is not, no action is needed and this can be ignored.

findings.title: Several pages share the same title
findings.evidence:
"Pumpkin Spice Latte Recipe" is the title of 2 pages:
    https://badseo.dev/content/duplicate-a
    https://badseo.dev/content/duplicate-b
findings.impact: Search engines use the title to tell pages apart. When several are identical they compete with each other for the same searches, and the one that wins is not necessarily the one you would choose.
findings.fix: Give each page a title naming what is specific to it, such as the product, the category or the location, before the business name.

findings.title: Several pages show word-for-word the same content
findings.evidence:
2 pages have identical body text:
    https://badseo.dev/content/duplicate-a
    https://badseo.dev/content/duplicate-b
    beginning "The same latte recipe, twice This page is identical, byte for byte, to another U…"
findings.impact: When the same text is published at more than one address, search engines pick one to show and largely ignore the rest, and the choice is theirs rather than yours. Any links pointing at the copies count for less than they would if everything pointed at one page.
findings.fix: Keep one address as the real one and either remove the duplicates or add a canonical link on each copy pointing at it. Where the pages are meant to differ, the shared text is the thing to change.

findings.title: Links to this site look plain when shared
findings.evidence: Missing og:title, og:description, og:image on https://badseo.dev/
findings.impact: When someone shares the link on WhatsApp, Facebook or LinkedIn, these tags decide whether it appears as a picture with a headline or as a bare URL. A bare URL gets noticeably fewer clicks.
findings.fix: Add `og:title`, `og:description` and an `og:image` of about 1200×630 to the shared layout, defaulting to the business logo where a page has no image of its own.

findings.title: A page leads nowhere else on the site
findings.evidence:
https://badseo.dev/privacy
    links to exactly one other page of this site: https://badseo.dev/
findings.impact: A visitor who lands here from search has nowhere relevant to go next, so they leave. For a search engine it is the end of a path, which means any page reachable only from here is reachable from nowhere at all.
findings.fix: Add links onward that suit the page: the section it belongs to, related items, or the next step in whatever the visitor came to do. Site-wide navigation counts, but only if it is actually rendered on this page.

findings.title: The page title is cut off in search results
findings.evidence:
110 characters on https://badseo.dev/head/title-too-long:
    "The Complete And Fully Unabridged Guide To Writing Page Titles That Are Much Too Long To Fit In Search Results"
findings.impact: Google truncates titles at roughly 60 characters, so the end of this one is replaced with an ellipsis. If the distinguishing words are at the end, searchers never see them.
findings.fix: Shorten to under 60 characters, putting the words that distinguish this page first and the business name last.

findings.title: The page title is very short
findings.evidence:
2 characters on https://badseo.dev/head/title-too-short:
    "Hi"
findings.impact: A short title gives searchers little reason to click and gives search engines little to match a query against.
findings.fix: Expand to roughly 50–60 characters describing what the page offers.

findings.title: The page has no description for search results
findings.evidence: No <meta name="description"> on https://badseo.dev/head/missing-meta-description
findings.impact: The description is the grey text under the blue link. Without one, Google pulls an arbitrary sentence from the page, often a cookie notice or a menu. It does not affect ranking, but it affects how many people click.
findings.fix: Add a `<meta name="description">` of 50–160 characters describing the page as a sentence a customer would read.

findings.title: The search-result description is cut off
findings.evidence:
215 characters on https://badseo.dev/head/meta-description-too-long:
    "This meta description keeps going well past the point where a search engine would ever show the whole thing, adding clause after clause after clause, so most of it ends up cut off …"
findings.impact: Anything past roughly 160 characters is replaced with an ellipsis, so a call to action at the end is never seen.
findings.fix: Trim to under 160 characters.

findings.title: The search-result description is very short
findings.evidence:
45 characters on https://badseo.dev/head/meta-description-too-short:
    "A short, unique snippet for this one fixture."
findings.impact: A description this brief leaves most of the space Google gives it unused, and gives a searcher little reason to choose this result over the one above it. Under roughly 50 characters, Google is also more likely to discard it and pull its own sentence from the page instead.
findings.fix: Expand to 50–160 characters, describing what the page offers as a sentence a customer would read.

findings.title: The page has several main headings
findings.evidence:
This line is an H1

So is this one

And this is the third H1

on https://badseo.dev/head/multiple-h1
findings.impact: With several top-level headings the page’s subject is ambiguous, and the outline a screen reader announces becomes flat.
findings.fix: Keep one `<h1>` and demote the rest to `<h2>`.

findings.title: Heading levels skip a step
findings.evidence:
On https://badseo.dev/head/heading-order-skip, an <h4> follows an <h1>:
    "The first section, which should have been an H2"
findings.impact: Headings are the document outline. Skipping a level breaks how screen readers let a user jump through the page, and muddies which sections belong to which.
findings.fix: Choose heading levels by position in the outline, not by how large you want the text to look. Set size with CSS.

findings.title: Some links pass through several redirects
findings.evidence:
https://badseo.dev/redirect/chain-1
      301 → https://badseo.dev/redirect/chain-1
      301 → https://badseo.dev/redirect/chain-2
      200 → https://badseo.dev/
findings.impact: Each hop adds a round trip before anything appears, which is most noticeable on a phone. Search engines also pass slightly less ranking credit through each additional hop.
findings.fix: Update the links to point at the final address, and collapse the server rules so one redirect reaches the destination.

findings.title: Some images have no text alternative
findings.evidence:
1 of 1 images on https://badseo.dev/content/images-missing-alt have no alt attribute:
    https://badseo.dev/img/placeholder.svg
findings.impact: A blind visitor hears nothing where the image is, and the image cannot appear in image search. Note that an empty `alt=""` is correct for purely decorative images. These have no attribute at all.
findings.fix: Add `alt` text describing what the image shows. For decorative images, add `alt=""` explicitly so assistive technology knows to skip them.

findings.title: Several pages share the same search-result description
findings.evidence:
"The same latte recipe, published word for word at two different URLs, so a search engine has to pick one and d…" appears on 2 pages:
    https://badseo.dev/content/duplicate-a
    https://badseo.dev/content/duplicate-b
findings.impact: Identical descriptions make every result look the same in a list, so searchers cannot tell which page answers their question.
findings.fix: Write a description per page, or generate one from the page’s own content.

findings.title: A page has very little text
findings.evidence: About 146 words of body text on https://badseo.dev/head/missing-title
findings.impact: Pages with little text rarely rank for anything beyond the business name, because there is nothing for a search engine to match a query against. Legitimate for a contact or login page; a problem for a page meant to attract visitors.
findings.fix: If this page is meant to bring in search traffic, expand it to answer the questions a customer would actually ask. If it is not, no action needed.

positives: Every page is set up to display properly on phones.
Every page declares the language it is written in.
A sitemap is declared in robots.txt, which helps search engines find every page.
